title: Toolbelt Assembly Workflow (scratch)
content:
TL;DR: rough brainstorm for a lightweight ‘Toolbelt’ UX that lets end-users combine small assistant tools (search, calculator, code-run, cite, summarizer) into ephemeral workflows. Goal: reduce roundtrips, surface curated tool combos, and balance token/cost impact with latency. This is a personal sketchpad — lots of open questions; intended for quick alignment before carving a narrower PRD.

Problem / motivation:
- Many product teams want predictable, composable assistant behaviors (e.g., search->summarize->format) without building full orchestration.
- Current approaches are either: hard-coded orchestrations in backend pipelines (inflexible) or multi-step prompts that cause chat churn and higher token cost.
- Users expect small utility tools (math, domain lookup, citation) to be chained cheaply with clear cost/latency tradeoffs.

Target user archetypes:
- Power users inside apps (productivity, CRMs) who assemble quick workflows for repetitive tasks.
- Customer engineers building integration templates for customers.
- End users who prefer a guided combo (e.g., convert meeting notes -> extract actions -> assign).

High-level goals / success metrics:
- Time-to-first-successful-chain <= 45s for 90% of test chains (hosted infra).
- Median token cost per two-step chain <= 1.6x single-step baseline.
- 30% of early adopter teams use prefabs (prebuilt tool combos) after 4 weeks.
- Fewer than 5% of chains trigger manual intervention (errors/fallbacks) in canary.

Core concept:
- Toolbelt: a small palette UI of tool tiles (card with icon, short name, expected latency/cost badge).
- Assembly canvas: drag-and-drop to connect tools into a linear chain (or forked branches later).
- Execution modes: interactive (step-by-step, human-in-loop confirmation), headless (execute chain end-to-end), and preview (dry-run that reports estimated cost/latency without executing).
- Prefabs: curated starting templates (e.g., research-summary, invoice-extractor, code-run+test).

User stories (examples):
- As a product power user, I want to combine ‘web-search’ + ‘summarizer’ so I can paste a URL and get a 3-bullet summary with sources.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to save a toolbelt prefab for client onboarding tasks and share it with teammates.
- As a developer, I want to see token/cost estimates before running a chain in headless mode.

Rough UX flow:
1) Open toolbelt drawer in app (keyboard shortcut to open).
2) Drag 'Search' tile to canvas; set scope (site: example.com) and result depth (top 3).
3) Drag 'Summarize' tile after search; pick tone/length; toggle include-citations.
4) Optional: insert 'Rewrite for Email' tile, choose persona.
5) Click Run -> preview pane shows per-step estimated tokens, likely latency, and a small confidence indicator.
6a) If interactive: present result from step 1 in a panel, allow user to accept/skip then continue to step 2.
6b) If headless: execute steps sequentially, aggregate final output and citations.

Technical considerations / constraints:
- Routing: prefer in-region execution for lower latency; some tiles may require specific model variants (e.g., code-run -> private dedicated instances).
- Batching & KV caching: cache search results / downloaded context as prefix to avoid re-fetching during preview/interactive runs.
- Fallbacks: if a tile times out, option to fallback to smaller model or partial output. Need policy config per prefab (cost cap, latency cap, fallback).
- Security: tool tiles that access external systems (calendar, drive) must flow through customer's private connector in Private/Dedicated deployments — surface connector requirements in tile metadata.
- Observability: per-chain trace ID, step-level latency and token usage, and a quick error taxonomy for operator dashboards.

Implementation sketch (MVP):
- Backend: orchestration microservice that compiles a linear chain into a sequence of Redwood API calls. Each step has a spec: model_hint, max_tokens, timeout_ms, required_connectors.
- Frontend: lightweight React canvas with a small tile palette; save prefab as JSON blob (name, tiles, step-params, policy).
- Storage: user-prefabs in hosted metadata store; team-prefabs flagged with sharing ACLs.

Rollout plan (canary -> beta -> GA):
- Internal dogfood: enable on Redwood Console for 2 internal teams (SE and Docs).
- Canary: opt-in for 10 customer accounts with engineering support. Collect failure modes and cost telemetry.
- Beta: add prefabs marketplace and sharing; 3-week closed beta with 20 customers.

Open questions / risks:
- How to present accurate cost estimates for steps that themselves fan-out (e.g., parallel searches)?
- UX complexity: balancing flexibility vs cognitive load (we should limit MVP to linear chains of <=4 steps).
- Data residency & connectors: what is minimum wiring to indicate a tile requires Private deployment?
- Billing model: per-step token-based charging vs per-chain overhead — interplay with Reserved/Dedicated.

Next steps (short list):
- Align with infra on an orchestration proto (Diego)
- Quick mockups + keyboard flow (Maya)
- Draft minimal step-spec schema (Lena)
- Identify 3 candidate prefabs for initial dogfood (research-summary, invoice-scan, meeting-recap)
- Create a JIRA epic and link prototype PRs

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep tile API very small: {id, name, description, inputs, outputs, model_hint, timeout_ms, cost_bucket}.
- Consider a 'preview token' that reserves a rough cost estimate from billing service before headless run.
- Add a 'safety checkbox' for connectors that access PII – require explicit consent per run.

Random brainstorm snippets:
- Could expose 'conditional' tiles (if bullet count > X then route to 'compress' tile). Save for v2.
- Marketplace idea: third parties publish tiles with vetted performance profiles (needs trust model).
- Tiny keyboard microflows: open + type ":research gmail thread" -> auto-assemble prefab search->summarize->tag.

End of scratch — capture again after internal sync on 2025-12-05.
__notes: informal scratchpad; do not use as final spec
